chunks.adarle20:overview:
A Darle 20 — A Darle 20
A marketplace for tabletop game sessions in Latin America. Live at adarle20.com. Sidhant's role: co-founder and CTO (solo developer).
chunks.adarle20:what-he-built:
A Darle 20 — What he built
He architected and shipped the product end to end: host profiles, session listings, bookings and reservations, real-time chat, email notifications, refunds, and authentication. Payments run on Stripe Connect, handling host payouts and platform fees … The funnel is instrumented end to end (bookings, conversion, cancellations, refunds, host activation), and that data steers product and monetization decisions.
He runs an AI-agent-heavy development workflow in Claude Code. Agents write most of the code, and he keeps hands-on ownership of architecture, product decisions, code review, and release. Later he set up a multi-agent workflow that reviews, refactors, and regression-tests the codebase on its own.
chunks.adarle20:where-it-stands:
A Darle 20 — Where it stands
Development started in August 2025; the platform launched in March 2026. Four months in, it has 1,400+ registered users, 127 hosts, and 2,100+ bookings …. The biggest single test so far was a flagship 251-player event at a 19,000-attendee convention, rated 4.96/5 by attendees. He built the technology behind it, and his co-founder ran the event on the ground. Running A Darle 20 has taught Sidhant as much about unit economics as about code. They've tested a commission model against direct event ticket sales and made decisions about where the margin is.
chunks.dell:overview:
Dell — Sales prediction at Dell
A propensity model for cross-sell targeting, built as an intern. Sidhant's role: marketing intern. 2018.
During a summer internship in 2018, Sidhant built a propensity model (Azure ML) on Dell's historical customer database to identify cross-sell targets for a high-margin software product. It surfaced about 20,000 qualified accounts representing an estimated $129M in pipeline, based on segment-level average deal sizes. The model was hosted on Azure so sales and marketing teams could get predictions and feed back new training data.
It was an internship project, but it's where he first got interested in work that combines data, revenue, and tooling, and he's been doing that kind of work since.
chunks.faq:what-does-he-bring-to-delivery-opera:
FAQ — What does he bring to delivery operations?
His titles have been sales operations and workforce management, not delivery operations. What follows is the work in his record that the role draws on, all of it stated elsewhere in this knowledge base.
Headcount and forecasting: as a workforce management specialist at Nokia (Oct 2022 – Jun 2024), he owned headcount reporting and forecasting for a 3,000–4,000-person organization, and identified $1.2M in real-estate cost savings by analyzing lab and facility utilization data.
Rollout and support: at Nokia he owns every tool through its full lifecycle, from vague requests from sales and finance leadership to scoped requirements, executive demos, global rollout, user support, and iteration across time zones.
Operating cadence: quarterly executive reporting runs on a self-serve Power App he built, used by 80+ stakeholders across 7 regions. It replaced a manual process that took one finance analyst's entire workday, every day of quarter-end close.
Running a live service: at A Darle 20 he integrated Stripe Connect for host payouts and platform fees …, with automated refunds, and instrumented the funnel (bookings, conversion, cancellations, refunds, host activation). He built the technology behind a 251-player event at a 19,000-attendee convention, rated 4.96/5 by attendees; his co-founder ran the event on the ground.
chunks.faq:what-roles-is-he-targeting:
FAQ — What roles is he targeting?
Revenue operations (RevOps / GTM systems) and delivery operations roles at AI-forward companies.
chunks.nokia:the-problem:
Nokia — The problem
Quarterly executive reporting ran on manual data collection. The process consumed one finance analyst's entire workday, every day of quarter-end close, chasing inputs across regions and formats. At the same time, sales reporting lived in Salesforce Analytics, which the organization was moving away from.
chunks.nokia:what-he-built:
Nokia — What he built
He built a self-serve Power App for quarterly executive reporting, now used by 80+ stakeholders across seven regions. It replaced the manual collection process entirely. He also owned the migration of all sales reporting from Salesforce Analytics to Power BI for 150+ users: data modeling, transformation logic in SQL and DAX, and the global rollout.
For both, he was the whole team: requirements, build, executive demos, user support, bug triage, and iteration across time zones. More recently he's been bringing LLMs and Python into these workflows where they help.
Note: this work is internal to Nokia, so screenshots and specifics are limited by confidentiality.
